summary: Stub package beacons installer host identifiers to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint on install and require
details: template-projection-map@22.1.1 is a functionally empty npm package whose only behavior is a reconnaissance beacon. The package.json postinstall hook executes beacon.cjs, which POSTs the installer's hostname (os.hostname()), install path (__dirname), current working directory (process.cwd()), and Node.js version to the hardcoded plain-HTTP bare-IP endpoint http://13.140.137.222:8787/_ah/dc. The same beacon is also fired from index.js at require() time via require('./beacon.cjs').fire(). index.js otherwise exports a Proxy whose every property returns a no-op, confirmed by the module's self-description as a Compatibility shim. The destination is a bare IPv4 address over cleartext HTTP, unrelated to any legitimate publisher infrastructure, and the package provides no advertised functionality that could justify such telemetry. The shape (install- and import-time outbound POST of host identifiers to an attacker-controlled endpoint on a stub/name-squat package) matches dependency-confusion reconnaissance tooling.
